Per-column merge rules for linked episodes

Source: R/utils-link-rules.R
resolve_merge_rules.Rd

When link_encounters() links an ED record and a separately submitted inpatient record into one episode, each column of the kept row is reconciled by a rule. The principle: only the HasBeen_ flags, C_Death and DispositionCategory are collapsed to one value so the row reflects the whole encounter of care; every other field keeps what either record holds.

Usage

resolve_merge_rules(data, merge_fields, table = merge_field_table)

is_informative(x, extra = NULL)

merge_prefer_primary(primary_value)

merge_prefer_informative(values, primary_value)

merge_earliest(values, primary_value)

merge_max(values, primary_value)

merge_linked_episodes(
  multi_row,
  rules,
  merge_delimiter,
  severity_col,
  has_been_cols
)

merge_union_delimited_all(x, ep, n_ep, delimiter)

Arguments

data

A data frame with the episode columns .episode_id and patient_class.

merge_fields

NULL, or a named character vector mapping column names (already in janitor::make_clean_names() form) to a strategy from merge_strategies. Each entry replaces the table's rule for that column.

table

The rule table; defaults to the internal merge_field_table. Exposed so tests can supply a small table.

x, values

A vector of one column's values.

extra

Extra text values to treat as uninformative for this column.

primary_value

The primary row's value.

multi_row

The rows of the episodes that have more than one row, with .episode_id, patient_class and, when present, .link_pull.

rules

The data frame returned by resolve_merge_rules().

merge_delimiter

The delimiter used by the "union_delimited" and "union_ccdd" strategies.

severity_col

The column merged with "prefer_severity", or NA.

has_been_cols

Names of the HasBeen_ flag columns, which take the maximum across an episode's rows.

Value

resolve_merge_rules() returns a data frame with one row per merged column: column, strategy, and follow (the column followed, or the text column whose length is recomputed, else NA). merge_linked_episodes() returns one row per episode. is_informative() returns a logical vector. The merge_*() functions return a single value.

Details

These helpers resolve and apply those rules.

  • resolve_merge_rules() assigns a strategy to every column that is merged. A column named in merge_fields uses that strategy. Otherwise the column is looked up in the internal merge_field_table (built from data-raw/merge_field_classification.csv, which follows the NSSP ESSENCE data dictionary) by its janitor::make_clean_names() name, then by a looser spelling (lower case, no underscores) when that spelling points to exactly one table row, so c_biosense_id finds C_BioSense_ID. Anything else follows its type: text keeps both records' values ("concat"), everything else takes the first informative value ("prefer_informative").

  • merge_linked_episodes() applies the rules to the rows of every multi-row episode and returns one row per episode. The rules that need no per-episode logic are computed over whole columns at once, and only the text-merging rules visit episodes one at a time.

  • is_informative() says which values carry information: a missing value, blank text, or a placeholder such as "None" or "Unknown" does not.

  • merge_prefer_primary(), merge_prefer_informative(), merge_earliest() and merge_max() are the one-episode versions of the matching strategies; merge_linked_episodes() must agree with them.

Rules that need a winning record use the primary row (the ED record when the episode has one, otherwise its first row). A column that takes "the winning record's value unless it is uninformative" takes the primary row's value, or, when that is missing or a placeholder, the first informative value from another record.

Two kinds of rule tie a column to another column's winning record, so values that belong together never mix records. "prefer_informative_disposition" (discharge and death times) uses the record that won DispositionCategory as its winning record. "follow" (units, derived lookups, durations) takes the value from whichever record supplied the column it follows, even when that value is missing: a weight and its units, or a zip code and its region, always come from one record. A column whose source is absent from the data falls back to the first informative value.

"recompute_length" sets CCOrig_Length, CCParsed_Length and DD_Length to the number of characters (separators included) in the merged ChiefComplaintOrig, ChiefComplaintParsed and DischargeDiagnosis. When the length column is present but its text column is not, the winning record's value is kept and a warning says so.
